tools.name: stop-simulator-server
tools.description: Stop the transport session for a specific device (iOS simulator / Android: simulator-server process; physical iOS: the on-device runner; Chromium: CDP WebSocket) and free its resources; on a TV target it also reaps that device's TV-control daemons. Use to restart a wedged transport, or when the user is done with one device but wants to keep others running - not just because a task on it finished, since the next task on that device would start cold again. On iOS / Android / TV it deliberately leaves this device's native-devtools, accessibility, profiler and debugger services running - to drain those as well, use stop-all-simulator-servers with `devices`. On CHROMIUM that does not hold: the JS-runtime debugger declares the CDP session as a dependency, so stopping the transport cascades to it and its captured console history goes with it - reconnect with debugger-connect afterwards. Returns { stopped, udid }. Fails silently if no session is open for the given id.

udid.description: Target device id (iOS UDID, Android serial, or Chromium id) whose transport session to stop

tools.name: stop-all-simulator-servers
tools.description:
Stop the services a device owns - simulator-server processes (iOS + Android), native devtools, the iOS accessibility service, TV-control daemons, Chromium CDP sessions, screen recordings, native profiler sessions, and JS-runtime debugger sessions along with the network inspectors and React profiler sessions that ride on them - freeing their spawned processes, sockets and ports. Call this when the user asks to clean up or ends the session, or when a skill tells you to recycle a device's services mid-flow - not just because a task finished, since the next task reuses these services and would start cold again.
PASS `devices` with the device ids this session used: one tool-server serves every agent, subagent and CLI call using this argent install, and an unscoped call tears down THEIR devices too (a mid-recording devtools teardown degrades another agent's e2e test to brittle coordinate taps; that agent is warned, but its recorded steps are already the worse kind). Omit `devices` only when a machine-wide cleanup is what you actually want. Passing an EMPTY array scopes to nothing and stops nothing - it is not a way to ask for the machine-wide sweep.
A JS-runtime debugger session is keyed by the id you called `debugger-connect` with. On a Metro serving two or more devices that id is not a udid or serial - connect refuses those and tells you to re-target with the `logicalDeviceId` it returns - so a scope built from `list-devices` ids cannot reach that session. Pass any such `logicalDeviceId` in `devices` ALONGSIDE the device id; { left_running } names the ones you missed.
Returns { stopped } - the URNs of the services that were actually live and got shut down; an ERROR node is disposed too but never appears there, so an empty `stopped` only means nothing was still running. { unmatched } lists supplied ids that own no service here, so a mistyped id - or a device NAME passed where an id was expected - does not read as a clean machine. It is NOT proof the id is wrong: a Vega device is driven through CLI/adb shell-outs, so one you only booted and drove with the remote registers no service and always lands here, as does a real device of any platform this session never started anything on. Present ONLY when `devices` was supplied AND at least one id matched nothing - absent on an unscoped call and when every id matched. Stopping the same device twice does not report it unmatched: ownership counts regardless of service state. { left_running } lists the URNs of live debugger sessions (and the network inspectors / React profiler sessions riding on them) whose id no device scope can name - re-call with the id after each URN's `<namespace>:<port>:` prefix to reap them. { aborted: true } means the caller cancelled the request part-way, so the rest of the machine was left untouched and neither of the other two fields was computed. Past the schema - which rejects an unknown key outright, so the `udids` slip is an error rather than a silent machine-wide sweep - the call always succeeds; reaping nothing is a result, not a failure.

devices.description: Device ids (iOS UDID / Android serial / Chromium id) to scope the teardown to. Pass the devices THIS session actually used. Omit only for a deliberate machine-wide cleanup: one tool-server serves every agent using this argent install, so an unscoped stop also kills devices another agent is mid-session on.

tools.name: stop-metro
tools.description: Stop the Metro bundler process listening on a given port (default 8081). Use when the user asks to stop Metro or when Metro must be restarted - do not offer it when a task wraps up, since the next task would wait on a cold Metro start. Returns { stopped, port, pids }; stopped=false if no process is found on the port. Fails if the port lookup command times out or the process cannot be killed. This is DESTRUCTIVE: always ask the user for confirmation before calling this tool.

port.description: TCP port Metro is listening on (default 8081)

tools.name: e2e-start-recording
tools.description:
Start recording a new e2e test, resetting .argent/e2e/<name>.yaml to an empty e2e test and replacing any existing one.
Use when you want to capture a reusable sequence of device interactions for later replay.
Returns { message, flowFile, savedTo } and optionally { restarted, discardedSteps } if a live recording of the same e2e test was discarded.
Without a link, it creates that file and fails if the .argent/e2e/ directory cannot be created or the file cannot be written. Over a link (argent link or ARGENT_TOOLS_URL, also to 127.0.0.1), your client writes the file, and `savedTo` is its path on your computer, or null when that write failed.

Several e2e tests can be recorded at once, each keyed by the `name` + `project_root`
that every subsequent recording tool repeats, and one recording's steps never
land in another's file. Steps still run LIVE, so give each concurrent recording
its own device and pick a name unique to your task.

After starting, use e2e-add-step to append tool calls. Each step is executed
LIVE so you can verify it works before it gets recorded. Read each step's
`message`: an await-ui-element whose condition never held is still recorded (it
returns success:false rather than failing), and a check that passes live can
still fail once polished into an `await:`/`assert:` directive, which resolves
against a different tree. e2e-add-step warns about both when you record the
wait DIRECTLY. A wait nested inside a recorded run-sequence gets neither warning
(that tool reports its own shape), so for those, read `toolResult`. For a standalone
e2e test, record a restart-app of the app under test as the FIRST step (captured
as the e2e test's `launch` step); for a reusable fragment, skip that and pass
executionPrerequisite instead. Use e2e-add-echo to add labels, and
e2e-add-script to run a local .mjs file and record it as a `script:` step.
Call e2e-finish-recording when done.

If a recorded step turns out to be wrong, edit the .yaml file directly to
remove or reorder steps - after e2e-finish-recording, not during the
recording. Over a link, the next recorded step writes over your edit.
Without a link, the recorder reads the file again before each step, but an
edit that renumbers the steps drops the warnings that e2e-finish-recording
reports for those steps.

name.description: Name for this e2e test (e.g. "settings-explore"): letters, digits, underscore and hyphen only.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the project root directory (the directory that contains or should contain `.argent/e2e/`). The e2e test file is created at `<project_root>/.argent/e2e/<name>.yaml`.

executionPrerequisite.description: Fragments only: the app/device state assumed on entry (e.g. "Settings app open on General page"). For a standalone e2e test, omit this and record a `restart-app` as the first step instead; it is captured as the e2e test's `launch` step. restart-app has no chromium support, so a chromium e2e test records as a fragment; add the `launch: { chromium: <app path> }` line to the YAML afterward, deleting the executionPrerequisite line if you passed one, since an e2e test that starts with a launch must not declare it.

tools.name: e2e-add-step
tools.description:
Execute one MCP tool and record its step in the e2e test named by `name` + `project_root`. Use when recording and you want each action run and captured; the recording must already be open.
A coordinate `gesture-tap` records as a portable `tap` selector step; `restart-app` as a `launch`.
Returns { message, stepCount, recorded, savedTo }; `recorded`, not the status, says whether a step was appended. Fails with an error, recording nothing. Call recording tools, including `e2e-add-script`, directly.

name.description: Name of the e2e test being recorded: the one passed to e2e-start-recording.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the project root of the e2e test being recorded: the same value passed to e2e-start-recording. Together with `name` it identifies which recording this step belongs to.

command.description: MCP tool to execute and record, for example "gesture-tap". Do not pass an e2e test directive or a recording tool. Call e2e-add-script directly for a requested script step.

args.description: Tool arguments as a JSON string, e.g. '{"udid": "ABC", "x": 0.5, "y": 0.3}'. Omit for tools with no arguments.

delayMs.description: Milliseconds to sleep before executing this step during replay.

tools.name: e2e-add-echo
tools.description:
Record an echo step in the e2e test named by `name` + `project_root`. Echo steps print a message when the e2e test is replayed, useful as labels between tool calls.
Use when you want to annotate a recorded e2e test with a human-readable label or checkpoint message.
Returns { message, stepCount, savedTo }. Fails if that e2e test has no recording in progress.

name.description: Name of the e2e test being recorded: the one passed to e2e-start-recording.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the project root of the e2e test being recorded: the same value passed to e2e-start-recording. Together with `name` it identifies which recording this echo belongs to.

message.description: Message to echo when the e2e test is replayed

tools.name: e2e-add-script
tools.description: Run a local .mjs file and record it as a `script:` step in an active e2e test. Use when the user requests a local script in the e2e test, and only then. Pass the same `name` and `project_root` as `e2e-start-recording`, and call it where the script must run. Returns `status`, `reason` and `stepCount`. A failed script is not recorded. Check `reason` and the affected state before you retry. Over a link (argent link or ARGENT_TOOLS_URL), the tool refuses the call: record such an e2e test with no link.

name.description: E2E test name passed to e2e-start-recording.

project_root.description: Absolute project root passed to e2e-start-recording.

path.description: Path to the .mjs file, relative to the e2e test YAML. For example: "../../scripts/seed-order.mjs".

timeout.description: Optional time limit in milliseconds. The default is 30000 and the minimum is 100.

tools.name: e2e-finish-recording
tools.description:
Finish recording the e2e test named by `name` + `project_root`, leaving recordings under any other key untouched. Returns { message, path, executionPrerequisite, steps, summary, flowFile, savedTo } - a summary of all recorded steps plus the final YAML. Use when you have added all desired steps and want to finalize the e2e test file. Fails if that e2e test has no recording in progress.
A warning e2e-add-step raised on a recorded `await-ui-element` is repeated in `summary` as a `warning:` line of its own, right below the step it judges, and `message` counts them by kind. A warning is repeated only while the step it judges is still identifiable by its number: hand-editing the .yaml during the recording moves the steps, so those warnings are DROPPED rather than pinned on whichever step inherited the number, and `message` says how many were dropped. A step that carries a cross-tree warning was re-probed against the runner's tree: read it before converting that wait to `await:`/`assert:`, which is what the verdict is about and what this moment is for. A step that recorded a wait which did not pass was never probed at all, and its own warning names the CAUSE, because only one of them judges the condition: an unmet wait was read and found false, and it stops the run at replay; a wait whose tree source could not be read, or one that was cancelled, observed nothing and leaves the condition UNKNOWN rather than known-bad. Read those before replaying.
You can still edit the .yaml file directly afterwards to remove or reorder steps.

name.description: Name of the e2e test being recorded: the one passed to e2e-start-recording.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the project root of the e2e test being recorded: the same value passed to e2e-start-recording. Together with `name` it identifies which recording to finish.

tools.name: e2e-read-prerequisite
tools.description:
Read the execution prerequisite of an e2e test without running it: a saved e2e test from the .argent/e2e/ directory (or the older .argent/flows/), or an explicit boundary-managed flow_path.
Returns { flow, executionPrerequisite, warning? }: the logical name, plus the precondition its author recorded
verbatim. Empty when none was declared, which is always so for a self-contained scenario: one opening
on a launch may declare no prerequisite, because it builds its own start state.
Use when deciding whether the device already sits where a fragment expects it (correct app foregrounded,
correct account, correct screen) before committing to a run, or when relaying that requirement to a human.
Touches no device: nothing is launched, tapped, dispatched or torn down, and no simulator or emulator
needs booting, so calling this costs nothing but a file read.
Fails if the e2e test file does not exist.
Address the e2e test exactly as you will address it in e2e-execute: name or flow_path, one and only one; supplying both or neither is rejected. The name goes in `name`, which resolves <project_root>/.argent/e2e/<name>.yaml, else .argent/flows/<name>.yaml.

name.description: Name of a saved e2e test to inspect from `.argent/e2e`, or `.argent/flows` when it is not there (e.g. "settings-explore"). Omit when flow_path is set.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the calling agent's project root: the cwd it is working in. With name, the saved e2e test is read from `.argent/e2e/<name>.yaml`, else `.argent/flows/<name>.yaml`, under this root; with flow_path, the prerequisite is read from that YAML instead, so pass the agent's cwd.

flow_file.description: Path to the e2e test .yaml as readable by the tool-server. Internal: the argent client derives it from project_root and name automatically; leave unset.

flow_path.description: Omit when name is set. Absolute path to an e2e test .yaml on the client. Over a link (argent link or ARGENT_TOOLS_URL), the argent client uploads the file and the tool-server reads the uploaded copy; without a link, the tool-server reads the file in place. Pass the path through the argent client; a raw path that the file-input boundary did not verify is rejected. Pass the same e2e test source here as to e2e-execute, so the prerequisite you read belongs to the e2e test that will run.

tools.name: e2e-execute
tools.description:
Run a saved YAML e2e test end to end. Use when
asked to replay a recorded path, re-run a QA regression, or check that a known journey still passes; for a
one-off interaction use the gesture tools instead, and to author an e2e test use e2e-start-recording. Pass
exactly one e2e test source: name (under project_root) or flow_path.
Returns a per-step report: the first failure stops the run and the rest report as skipped.

name.description: Name of a saved e2e test to run from `.argent/e2e`, or `.argent/flows` when it is not there (e.g. "settings-explore"). Omit when flow_path is set.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the calling agent's project root: the cwd it is working in. With name, the saved e2e test is read from `.argent/e2e/<name>.yaml`, else `.argent/flows/<name>.yaml`, under this root; with flow_path, the e2e test, its run: siblings, its script: paths and baselines all resolve beside the YAML instead, so pass the agent's cwd. A script still RUNS in this root whichever source was used.

flow_file.description: Path to the e2e test .yaml as readable by the tool-server. Internal: the argent client derives it from project_root and name automatically; leave unset.

flow_path.description: Omit when name is set. Absolute path to an e2e test .yaml on the client. Over a link (argent link or ARGENT_TOOLS_URL), the argent client uploads the file, its run: fragments and the snapshot baselines of each run, and the tool-server runs those copies. Keep run: fragments under project_root or beside the e2e test file. With updateBaselines, the client writes the new baselines when the run ends. The client also uploads each absolute .png or .yaml path that a tool: step takes as a file argument, when the file is under project_root or beside the e2e test file. A tool: e2e-execute step that names an e2e test with name and an absolute project_root without a .. segment runs: the client also uploads that e2e test and its own files. Over a link, the uploaded e2e tests must not have: script: steps; tool: steps that run an e2e test another way or record an e2e test; tool: steps that take a directory, an app or an output directory; tool: steps whose tool builds a file path from several arguments; tool: steps that name a relative path or a file other than .png or .yaml. Without a link, the tool-server reads the files in place and all step kinds run.

device.description: Device id to run against (iOS UDID, Android/Vega serial, Chromium id), as list-devices reports it. Auto-detected when omitted, but only when exactly one booted device matches (optionally narrowed by `platform`); with several booted the run fails and lists them, so pass this explicitly whenever more than one device is up.

platform.description: Restrict auto-detection to this platform when several devices are booted. `ios` selects local simulators only; pass `ios-remote` to select a remote one. `chromium` does more than filter: with no `device` it SELECTS the self-boot branch for a standalone e2e test - the runner boots an Electron instance from the `launch` step's chromium value and tears it down after the run (a single-key `launch: { chromium: … }` map selects it on its own, without this parameter). When it selects that branch it never falls back to device auto-detection (a fragment, or a standalone e2e test's launch map with no `chromium` key, still does), and the launch value must be a real Electron app path on the tool-server host: a bare-string `launch:` - what the recorder writes - holds an installed-app bundle id, so passing `chromium` for one fails the whole run with `Electron boot: path does not exist`. Edit the launch to `{ chromium: <app path> }` first.

updateBaselines.description: Write/refresh screenshot baselines for `snapshot` steps instead of diffing against them, also in the e2e tests that tool: e2e-execute steps run, unless such a step sets updateBaselines itself.

prerequisiteAcknowledged.description: Set to true to confirm the execution prerequisite has been met. Required (LLM path) when a fragment defines an executionPrerequisite.

tools.name: update-argent
tools.description: Apply a pending Argent update. Only call this tool when the user has explicitly consented to updating Argent in this conversation. Use when an update notification indicates a new version is available and the user agrees to update. By default updates the install serving this session; pass `target` to choose global/local/both. Returns { message } with the update status and version info. The tool server will restart automatically after the update. Fails if no update is available or an update is already in progress.

target.description: Which install to update. 'auto' (default) updates the install serving this session: the global PATH install or this project's local devDependency, whichever this server runs from. Pass 'global' / 'local' to force one, or 'both' when the user has both and wants each updated.

tools.name: dismiss-update
tools.description: Clear the Argent update notification for the given number of hours. Use when the user asks to postpone or silence update reminders. Returns { message } confirming the suppression duration. Fails if the hours value is negative or the suppression state cannot be persisted.

hours.description: Number of hours to suppress the update notification
